artifacts.title: Peter Benyola v. Central Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC declared Benyola's complaint against Central Florida Presbytery administratively out of order and incapable of being put in order, because Benyola was no longer a member of any PCA congregation and thus lacked standing. The decision was adopted 23-0 on a roll call, one absent, on the officers' recommendation. The record does not identify the underlying presbytery action or reach the complaint's merits, so the case's value is its threshold standing ruling, not any complaint determination.

artifacts.synopsis: On a BCO 41 reference, the SJC tried a minister on seven charges arising from allegations of sexual misconduct, bullying, dishonesty, a civil defamation suit, contumacy, doctrinal error, and lack of fitness. It found him not guilty on every charge because the prosecution failed to meet its burden, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to good standing. For the lawsuit charge, it rejected a categorical ban on civil suits between Christians and required proof that this suit was sinful.

artifacts.synopsis: Ryan Speck challenged Missouri Presbytery’s BCO 31-2 investigation and its refusal to commence process against Greg Johnson on four allegations concerning same-sex attraction as sin, identity in Christ, sanctification, and fitness for office. The SJC denied the complaint in full. It found no clear procedural error and held that Johnson’s explanations and clarifications made Presbytery’s non-indictment judgments reasonable. No trial was ordered. The ruling neither adjudged Johnson guilty nor endorsed every statement or broader constitutional position concerning same-sex attraction.

artifacts.title: Art Sartorius et al. v. Siouxlands Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Teaching and ruling elders challenged Presbytery’s approval of TE Gregory Lawrence’s acquittal on five doctrinal charges. The SJC sustained the complaint on procedural grounds: the trial commission relied on his post-indictment exculpatory writings while he declined to testify, depriving the prosecution of cross-examination. The SJC ordered a new trial on the same indictment under specified evidentiary procedures. Because this was a complaint rather than an appeal, it did not reverse the acquittals into findings of guilt or decide the doctrinal merits.

artifacts.synopsis: Louisiana Presbytery’s refusal to institute process after examining Steve Wilkins’s Federal Vision teachings was challenged for applying the wrong constitutional standard and overlooking a strong presumption that some views were out of conformity with the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled Presbytery’s denial. A “difference” need not expressly contradict the Standards; Presbytery must independently investigate and classify it rather than accept the member’s assurance or shift the burden to objectors. The ruling did not adjudicate Wilkins’s guilt; the Central Carolina memorial remained before the SJC.

artifacts.synopsis: In a BCO 40-5 memorial, Central Carolina Presbytery alleged that Louisiana Presbytery had exonerated TE J. Steven Wilkins despite his published views on election, the church, perseverance, assurance, and baptism allegedly contradicting the Westminster Standards. The SJC sustained the memorial’s gravity and found Presbytery failed to show due diligence, ordering a recorded examination, formal responses, and report. Presbytery later met the procedural directives, but the SJC relied on Case 2007-8’s substantive finding, cited Presbytery under BCO 40-5, and appointed a prosecutor for Case 2007-14.

artifacts.synopsis: A presbytery annulled a session's actions after the session added to a petition-called congregational meeting a recommendation that the congregation invoke BCO 24-6 against eleven elders. The SJC sustained the session's complaint: BCO 25-2 permits a session to add agenda items, and BCO 24-6 does not require a member-initiated motion; the congregation's own 503–229 vote began the process. It reinstated the session's actions, declared remaining relief moot, and noted one recorded dissent; no dissent text appears.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC found Case 2003-6 judicially out of order because the challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery action was only advice in response to a BCO 41-1 reference from White Oak Session, not a binding or complainable doctrinal decision under BCO 41-3. The underlying dispute—whether elders could hold and teach a broader atonement view—was therefore not reached. The adopted vote was 17 concurring, 1 dissenting, with 1 abstention and 4 absent. The dissent argued Presbytery's 'not allowed' language read as compulsory final disposition.

artifacts.synopsis: Abshire challenged Presbytery’s commission for its appointment, scope, exhortation, summary disposition of two elders’ complaint, and other actions. The SJC sustained only the challenge to deciding the elders’ complaint without BCO 43 procedures and remanded that complaint. It denied the other issues: the commission could conduct the required investigation, the scope objection was untimely, and its exhortation and report were pastoral rather than formal discipline. A separate sixth issue remained before Presbytery and was not decided.

artifacts.title: Sang Bai Kim and RE Chan Soo Kim v. Korean Eastern Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: In a dispute arising from a Korean Eastern Presbytery congregational election, two ruling elders were tried, refused to plead, and were suspended from sacraments and office; KEP denied their appeal, then increased the censures to deposition and excommunication for contumacy. The SJC affirmed KEP's denial and the guilt findings, but reversed the increased censures. An appellate court may not increase a censure under BCO 42-9; the trial court retains discretion to remove or increase an indefinite suspension, though the appellate court may recommend a lesser censure. The original suspension remained.

artifacts.synopsis: The St. Paul Session and other Central Florida presbyters complained that Presbytery wrongly sustained a commission report denying the Session complaint and declining to find a strong presumption of guilt against Pastor John Hutchinson. The SJC denied the complaint on both issues. It held CFP permissibly directed a BCO 31-2 investigation and chose its own procedures; procedural irregularities and possible bias did not show BCO 39-3 clear error, though the panel criticized CFP’s handling. A lone dissent would remand, alleging the commission ignored the substance of 41 of 45 specifications.

artifacts.synopsis: New River Presbytery treated Grace Covenant PCA's BCO 41 inquiry about a Sunday school teacher's acceptability as a request for advice, but then ruled he was eligible to teach. On Harvestwood's complaint, the SJC held that Presbytery lacked original jurisdiction to make that final disposition and that the record was unclear about the teacher's views. The SJC sustained the complaint and recommended that Presbytery rescind its March 15, 1997 action and clarify his views through proper BCO procedures; it declined to reach the creation and theistic-evolution merits.

artifacts.synopsis: On Covenant Presbytery’s mixed BCO 41 reference, the SJC held that ministers Morse and Crenshaw could not resign unilaterally; joining another evangelical church invoked BCO 38-3, requiring their names erased, with notice that they were in good standing and faced no pending charges. Grace Church’s withdrawal required a congregational vote, not notice to Presbytery, so its name also was to be erased. Grace had abandoned its complaints, rendering them moot; the SJC nevertheless opined that recording a protest is insulated from complaint by BCO 45-5.

artifacts.synopsis: Heritage Presbytery adopted a committee report answering a session's reference on whether a session may require officers to abstain from beverage alcohol. Olson and others complained. The SJC held the complaint administratively out of order because it was not timely filed with the General Assembly, and independently ruled that a court's response to a non-judicial reference seeking advice under BCO 41-3 is not complainable. Complainants may submit their questions to the Committee on Constitutional Business. Confirmed 23-0.

artifacts.title: Power of a receiving court to broaden charges in a transferred judicial case

matches.evidence: When a judicial case is transferred, the receiving court becomes court of original jurisdiction and may add further charges pertaining to the original matter, but wholly new charges must go back to the first court.
